subject: Franska
title: Telling time and days of the week
sourceSummary: How to tell the time, days of the week and months, plus how to talk about a schedule.

questions.prompt: How do you ask "what time is it?" in French?
questions.opener: A fixed phrase you just need to memorize.
questions.explanation: "Quelle heure est-il ?" is the fixed phrase for "what time is it?".

questions.prompt: How do you say "it's three o'clock"?
questions.explanation: "Il est trois heures" is used for three o'clock. "Heures" is plural from two o'clock onward ("il est une heure" is the exception, in the singular).

questions.prompt: What does "neuf heures et demie" mean?
questions.explanation: "Et demie" means "and half", i.e. 30 minutes past: "neuf heures et demie" = 09:30 (half past nine).

questions.prompt: Which day of the week is "mercredi"?
questions.opener: The French week starts with Monday.
questions.explanation: "Mercredi" is Wednesday. Days of the week: lundi, mardi, mercredi, jeudi, vendredi, samedi, dimanche.

questions.opener: The name looks similar to the English one.
questions.explanation: "Décembre" is December. French month names are quite similar to the English ones.

questions.opener: Comes right before "dimanche" in the week.

questions.prompt: Correct the error: "Il a cinq heures de l'après-midi." (It's five in the afternoon.)
questions.opener: Time is always expressed with "être" (il est), not "avoir".
questions.answer: Il est cinq heures de l'après-midi.
steps: "Il a" is wrong — time must always be expressed with "il est" (être), never "il a" (avoir).
Full sentence: "Il est cinq heures de l'après-midi."

questions.prompt: How do you ask about and answer questions about time, days of the week, and months in French?
questions.opener: Fixed phrases for time, days, and months.
questions.answer: Time: Quelle heure est-il ? = What time is it? · Il est une heure = It's one o'clock · Il est deux/trois heures... = It's two/three o'clock... · et demie = and half · et quart = and a quarter · moins le quart = quarter to. Days of the week: lundi, mardi, mercredi, jeudi, vendredi, samedi, dimanche. Months: janvier, février, mars, avril, mai, juin, juillet, août, septembre, octobre, novembre, décembre.
